extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, and researchers interested in corporate collapses and scandals
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia list article that compiles historical and modern examples of corporate collapses (insolvencies/bankruptcies/nationalisations) and corporate scandals (alleged or actual unethical behaviour). It documents inclusion criteria and short descriptions of each case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate collapse (definition / inclusion criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: A corporate collapse typically involves the insolvency or bankruptcy of a major business enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion for the 'List of major corporate collapses' is described as corporations whose collapse involved major risk of job losses or size of the business, and which meant entering into insolvency or bankruptcy, or being nationalised or requiring a non-market loan by a government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate scandal (definition / inclusion criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: A corporate scandal involves alleged or actual unethical behavior by people acting within or on behalf of a corporation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article distinguishes scandals that do not involve insolvency (see 'List of scandals without insolvency'); many recent corporate collapses and scandals have involved false or inappropriate accounting. Scandals are included for alleged or actual unethical conduct even if the company did not become insolvent.
